suite_baseline: AI Governance Suite v3.9.10 (52 artefacts, AIG-xx IDs), Playbook AIG-GOV-02

not_collected: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (excluded)
coverage.statement: This observatory reads AI Incident Database (weekly Excel export) and Curated public-sector cases (cases.json). It does not read Find Case Law (UK court judgments) (licence-required); OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (excluded); AIAAIC Repository (unverified); Database of AI Litigation (DAIL) (unverified); ICO enforcement action (covered-elsewhere). Counts describe what these sources recorded, not how often failures happen in the world. Media-sourced incidents are allegations unless an authority made a finding.

modes.label: Performance failure or drift
modes.coverage_note: Performance monitoring, drift detection and the Post-Deployment Monitoring Log.

modes.label: Biased or discriminatory outcome
modes.coverage_note: Equality Impact Assessment before approval; bias and fairness monitoring after go-live.

modes.label: Harm to vulnerable people
modes.coverage_note: Vulnerable-residents escalation trigger, Human Rights Assessment and the Fundamental Rights Coverage Crosswalk.

modes.label: Unlawful or excessive personal data processing
modes.coverage_note: DPIA per use (UC-ID) before processing starts. Since v3.9.10 the DPIA and the Intake Form both record the record of processing (ROPA) reference.

modes.label: Hallucination or false content
modes.coverage_note: Generative AI guidance: human check before release and labelling of AI-generated content.

modes.label: Opaque decision nobody could explain
modes.coverage_note: Transparency Policy, ATRS Record and Model Card.

modes.label: Security compromise of or through the AI
modes.coverage_note: Security Review Checklist including agent threats; logging and incident detection controls.

modes.label: Solely automated significant decision
modes.coverage_note: Statutory-decision escalation trigger, DPIA covering UK GDPR Articles 22A to 22D, and the Contestability and Redress Control.

modes.label: Automation bias and over-reliance
modes.coverage_note: Human oversight controls and the human accountability principles.

modes.label: Agent acted beyond its authority
modes.coverage_note: Seventh escalation trigger (action without per-action human review), Agent Record, Authority Graph and Action Decision Record.

modes.label: Poor or unsuitable data
modes.coverage_note: Data quality requirements, data lineage standard and the Source Assurance and Traceability Register. Since v3.9.10 a Data Steward (AIG-AIMS-04 ROL-20) looks after data quality and lineage for each AI system, the AI Register links each system to its Information Asset Register entry (AIG-INV-04 column AA), and ISO/IEC 5259 and DAMA-DMBOK are recorded as voluntary references (AIG-AIMS-05 REQ-057, REQ-058).

modes.label: Unregistered or unauthorised use (shadow AI)
modes.coverage_note: Staff Guide, low-friction disclosure, retrospective intake and the AI Register.

modes.label: Reused for a purpose nobody assessed (function creep)
modes.coverage_note: Now covered: every materially distinct use gets its own UC-ID and approval applies only to the scope decided; the Statement of Applicability (A.9.4) requires scope-creep detection and reapproval; AIMS scope assigns downstream-use responsibility when the council provides AI to others.

modes.label: AI used to monitor or manage staff
modes.coverage_note: Unmapped: a search of all 52 artefacts found nothing on AI used to monitor or manage council staff. The suite governs AI as it affects residents; the council as employer is not covered.

modes.label: No accountable owner
modes.coverage_note: Named Service Owner per AIR-ID, Terms of Reference and the Governance Decision Record.

modes.label: Supplier opacity or failure
modes.coverage_note: Procurement and supplier governance policy and the Supplier Due Diligence Questionnaire.

modes.label: No route to challenge or redress
modes.coverage_note: Now covered: the Contestability and Redress Control applies wherever AI made or materially influenced a decision, routed through the council complaints procedure.

modes.label: Deployed without assessment
modes.coverage_note: Gate Map and Gate Log: no use proceeds without intake and the required delegated decision.

modes.label: Supplier changed the model underneath
modes.coverage_note: Now covered: material supplier or model change is an escalation trigger (minimum High), the Supplier DDQ asks how changes will be notified (Q7.1 and change-control annex), and the Model Card keeps a change history. Residual risk: detection still relies on the supplier telling the council; a silent change is only caught if post-deployment monitoring notices the behaviour shift.

modes.label: Deskilling and lost fallback capability
modes.coverage_note: Partial: §4.3.13 names degraded manual fallback as a risk and the Rollout Plan records a fallback, but nothing measures whether staff can still do the work unaided. AIMS-10 measure M-10 covers AIMS role competence only.

modes.label: Cumulative harm to the same people
modes.coverage_note: Partial: the portfolio view (§4.5.8, Capabilities and System Map, measure M-16) tracks risk concentration on the council's side, such as supplier dependency. It does not look across systems at whether the same residents or communities are carrying the combined burden.

gap_list.label: AI used to monitor or manage staff
gap_list.coverage_note: Unmapped: a search of all 52 artefacts found nothing on AI used to monitor or manage council staff. The suite governs AI as it affects residents; the council as employer is not covered.
